 Former Congressman Tim Holden has passed away at age 69. (U.S. HOUSE OF REPRESENTATIVES)
 By Ryan Sharp | rsharp@republicanherald.com PUBLISHED: November 15, 2026 at 2:40 PM EST | UPDATED: November 15, 2026 at 4:50 PM EST Getting your Trinity Audio player ready... Former Congressman Tim Holden, a Democrat who served Schuylkill County in the House of Representatives from 1993-2013, died Sunday at age 69.
 Holden was born in St. Clair in 1957 and graduated from St. Clair Area High School in 1975.
 He became sheriff of Schuylkill County in 1985 and served in that position until he was elected to represent Pennsylvania’s 6th Congressional District in 1992. He continued to serve as the representative of the redrawn 17th District until losing in the 2012 Democratic primary to Moosic attorney Matt Cartwright.
 Soon after leaving Congress in 2013, he was appointed by then-Gov. Tom Corbett to the Pennsylvania Liquor Control Board. Tom Wolf named Holden chairman of the PCLB in 2015, a position he held until retiring in November 2024 . Holden was the third person from Schuylkill County to chair the board.
 Tributes pour in
 Holden’s passing drew condolences from both sides of the political aisle, as local leaders and organizations expressed praise for Holden’s love and support for the region he served.
 “I am deeply saddened to hear of the passing of former Congressman Tim Holden. Respected across party lines, Tim was a champion of bipartisanship who believed in finding common ground. As one of the original Blue Dogs, he encouraged cooperation across the aisle and served our region with honor and integrity,” said U.S. Rep. Dan Meuser (R-9), who currently serves Schuylkill County in congress. “He will be missed, but his legacy of service will live on in the communities he represented. My prayers are with his family, friends, and all who knew and loved him.”
 Meuser recently won reelection against Rachel Wallace, a Schuylkill County native who served on Holden’s staff.
 “A lifelong son of Schuylkill County, Tim dedicated many years of his life to public service, representing our community in the United States Congress from 1993 to 2013,” the Pottsville City Democratic Committee said in a Facebook post. “His roots in our community and his commitment to serving the people of Schuylkill County will remain an important part of our area’s history. We are grateful for his years of service and his dedication to the people and communities he represented.”
 “Tim Holden served Schuylkill County well for many years, as our Sheriff, our Congressman, and as the PLCB Chairman,” state Sen. Dave Argall (R-29) said. “He helped a lot of people, whenever he could.”
 Palo Alto Mayor John Deatrich, who recently ran to represent Pennsylvania’s 123rd Legislative District, shared memories of Holden in a post.
 “I grew up in garages, I soaked in every conversation I overheard. (For better or worse, probably the latter). That being said, I made note of who spoke highly about Tim Holden,” he said. “The answer was everyone. What I found most interesting was that it was people from all backgrounds, all beliefs, all ages, all social demographics. People I saw rarely agree on anything, agreed on the fact that Tim Holden was a stand-up guy.”
 This is a developing story and will be updated as more information becomes available.
